parsed.basis: Botswana has no documented trans-specific criminal offence, and consensual same-sex conduct is lawful following the 2019 High Court decision, upheld on appeal in 2021 and formally removed from the Penal Code in 2026. Court rulings in 2017 required recognition of two transgender citizens' gender identities, although no clear administrative gender-marker process had been introduced by 2023. Employment law prohibits sexual-orientation discrimination, but same-sex partnerships are not recognised. Societal discrimination persists despite rising tolerance, while documented violence against trans people is absent from the available record and police have not been shown to target same-sex activity. No region-specific information distinguishes Ghanzi District from the national picture for a transgender visitor.
